items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: When Joe went with Basie, Basie had a blues-based band, and he stayed with that. So Joe had to fit in.

ctx.x: Now Joe has had this — during his career he’s had this blues thing. And sometimes, from what I’ve read, it was a little too pervasive and he wanted to be an all-around singer. And he almost got typecast.

Joe was a ballad singer to start. And then he liked some of the blues things and he started to use them on the South Side of Chicago. And he used the Memphis Slim song, “Every Day.” And Memphis Slim used to like to go hear him sing it, but Memphis said to me personally, when I interviewed him about Joe, he said, “Joe’s a pop singer.” You know? And he was. He was a balladeer and he sang the ballads mostly and that’s what he wanted to be known as. And Hank Jones the pianist bumped into him in the midwest before Joe…
Chicago was such a fertile city for music.
